web_blocks.title: Disclosing the facts-ledger vs. snapshot stage split

web_blocks.html: Our automated pipeline scripts disagree on the stage label, and we disclose that split transparently. The quantitative market-facts script tags MSTR as Stage 1 (Basing) solely because price sits within 0.01 ATR of its 63-day low ($77.69). Meanwhile, both the TradingView snapshot and the multi-timeframe options package classify MSTR as STAGE_4 with a CAP_REJECTED timing gate. Because price is 43.99% below a falling 50-day average and 40.95% below the 200-day average on nine distribution days, Stage 4 is the only honest operational reading.

Broad market and sector context confirm the risk-off backdrop. The S&P 500 sits in an official Downtrend regime, down 11.6% from its October 6 peak with 10 distribution days and only 34.5% of screened stocks above their 50-day average. CBOE total put-call ratio reached 1.13 (SPX 1.41), signaling elevated hedging demand. Although TheWrap maps MSTR under Financial Conglomerates (91% outperforming S&P 500), only 38% of that industry sits above its 50-day or 200-day EMA, and MSTR shows no breakout. [43][52][53]

web_blocks.title: Why the old $88–$94 zone and $79.00 stop are obsolete

web_blocks.html: The prior November 12 dossier set a conditional $88 to $94 watch band and a $79.00 invalidation stop. Price sliced cleanly through both levels in six sessions, proving that falling knives do not respect static prior-cycle shelves. Similarly, the automated snapshot still displays a stale support zone of $120.56 to $140.99 derived from prior moving averages—far above the $77.80 close. Any future re-underwriting would require a multi-week base near $55 to $62 (around 0.70x to 0.75x EV/BTC mNAV), a $48.00 structural floor, and a weekly close back above a flattening 30-week SMA.

The options engine returns NO_OPTIONS_EDGE and blocks any bullish call or LEAPS spread. At $77.80, MSTR sits far below its 50-day and 200-day structural floors, and its CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL fundamental status does not qualify for counter-trend call buying. Note also that the Linux container cannot access a live macOS Chrome Robinhood or TradingView session, so options data came from public feeds while the positions ledger confirms zero open MSTR options.

web_blocks.title: TAPE DISCIPLINE
paragraphs: RSI at 20.22 (daily) and 14.33 (4-hour) can spark violent dead-cat bounces, especially ahead of MSCI's November 2026 index rebalance. Do not mistake short-covering spikes for Stage 2 accumulation. [2][42]

book_paragraphs: Reading the November 20, 2026 tape requires zero guesswork. MSTR closed at $77.80, down 9.67% for the session, 30.30% for the week, and 46.64% for the month. That slide broke right through the prior $88 to $94 watch band and breached the $79.00 structural stop from November 12. Even worse, the stock ended just eleven cents above its $77.69 intraday 52-week low, meaning there is no verified technical floor underneath current prices. [42]

Every moving average confirms a severe Stage 4 markdown. The 20-day SMA sits at $120.72, 35.6% overhead. The 50-day SMA sits at $138.91 and is falling, 44.0% above the close. The 200-day SMA stands at $131.76 and the 30-week SMA stands at $128.25, roughly 40% above current trading. Daily volume reached 35.72 million shares—1.95 times the 20-day average—marking the ninth distribution day in 25 sessions. Institutional sellers are liquidating into weakness rather than defending a floor. [42]

We must disclose an automated classifier disagreement in our data pipeline. The quantitative market-facts ledger tags MSTR as Stage 1 Basing because price sits right on its 63-day low of $77.69. By contrast, both the TradingView snapshot and our multi-timeframe options package assign STAGE_4 with a CAP_REJECTED timing gate. Looking at the underlying math—price 44% below a falling 50-day average, nine distribution days, and a 4-hour RSI of 14.33 with no upward turn—the Stage 4 classification is clearly right.

Macro breadth offers no shelter for high-beta crypto proxies. The S&P 500 entered an official Downtrend regime on November 20, down 11.6% from its October 6 record with ten distribution days and only 34.5% of stocks above their 50-day averages. A CBOE total put-call ratio of 1.13 shows broad institutional demand for downside protection. Against that backdrop, MSTR's 3.70 beta acts as an accelerant to the downside. [41][52][53]

Both the old $79.00 stop and the snapshot's stale $120.56 to $140.99 moving-average band are useless for new money today. In a vertical downtrend, a 20.22 daily RSI can trigger sharp one-day short-covering rallies, especially around MSCI's November 2026 exclusion window. Yet without a multi-week horizontal base—potentially down in the $55 to $62 range if forced selling persists—and a decisive reclaim of the 30-week average, buying weakness is speculation rather than Stage 2 investing. [2][42]

Finally, the options desk finds no actionable convexity trade. Because MSTR fails both the structural-trend floor and the COMPOUNDER_PASS quality bar, the automated playbook returns NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. Public options data were used because macOS browser automation is unavailable in this Linux workspace, and the same-session positions ledger confirms zero MSTR options held.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a stock breaks its prior structural stop on nearly double average volume, the tape has already voted. Wait for a multi-week base to form before risking capital.
